items.bewering: 'n Emosie is 'n gevoel wat vanself in jou opkom en weer wegraak.
items.bron: APA, Emotion (apa.org/topics/emotion): emotion is a reaction pattern to a personally significant event; APA Handbook (Dess 2010) as quoted: an emotion is 'a relatively brief episode'. Arising unbidden and passing is consistent with both. Simplified for Gr 4 (APA also includes bodily and behavioural parts), but not false.

items.bewering: Jy kies nie wanneer so 'n gevoel kom nie, en jy kan dit nie sommer laat ophou nie.
items.bron: Gross's emotion-regulation research (summarised at technav.ieee.org/topic/emotion-regulation; Mauss et al. 2006, ocf.berkeley.edu/~eerlab): suppression reduces how much shows but leaves the feeling intact, and regulation changes how long and how strongly an emotion runs rather than switching it off. 'Nie sommer' (not just like that) is the right strength. It does not say a feeling can never be eased, which the later blocks teach.

items.bewering: Soms sien 'n ander mens iets daarvan aan jou, en soms sien hy niks nie.
items.bron: Barrett et al. 2019, 'Emotional expressions reconsidered', Psychological Science in the Public Interest 20(1) (APS release psychologicalscience.org/news/releases/emotion-expressions-pspi.html): faces carry meaning but do not reliably show the feeling. Gross: suppression hides what shows.

items.bewering: Liefde is die warm gevoel vir iemand wat vir jou baie beteken. ... Jy voel dit net so by 'n maat of by 'n boetie. Jy wil naby daardie mens wees, en jy mis hom wanneer hy weg is.
items.bron: Attachment research (Brubacher & Johnson 2017, cls.unc.edu): a bond marked by seeking closeness and distress at separation. Nummenmaa et al. 2014, 'Bodily maps of emotions', PNAS (Aalto University summary, aalto.fi): love is felt as warmth over the body. Love for friends and siblings as well as grandparents is ordinary attachment.

items.bewering: 'warm gevoel' (liefde), 'ligte gevoel' (geluk), 'swaar gevoel' (hartseer)
items.bron: Mapping checked as a set. Nummenmaa et al. 2014 (PNAS; aalto.fi summary): emotions have distinct body-sensation maps that hold across cultures, and love feels warm. Paul Ekman Group, 'What is sadness?' (paulekman.com): sadness brings loss of muscle tone and a lowered posture, which matches 'heavy'. A learner who reasons further from these descriptions is not misled. They describe how the feeling seems, not a cause.

items.bewering: Geluk is die ligte gevoel wanneer iets goeds met jou gebeur. Jy voel dit ná 'n wedstryd of op 'n dag saam met vriende.
items.bron: APA (apa.org/topics/emotion): which emotion you feel depends on what the event means to you, and a good event brings enjoyment. Observation, not a fault: 'ná 'n wedstryd' is an example of an occasion, and a match only gives happiness if it went well. The block's own first sentence ('wanneer iets goeds met jou gebeur') limits it, so it is not false. The writer may sharpen it if they wish.

items.bewering: Baie kinders wil dadelik vir iemand vertel wat gebeur het.
items.bron: Gable, Reis, Impett & Asher 2004, JPSP (sas.rochester.edu): people tell others about good events ('capitalization'). Rimé's work on the social sharing of emotion (Wikipedia 'Social sharing of emotions', citing Rimé et al.): 88-96% of emotional experiences are shared, and in a 1996 study children aged 6 and 8 told their parents within hours. 'Baie kinders' is suitably modest.

items.bewering: Hartseer is die swaar gevoel wanneer jy iets verloor wat vir jou saak maak. 'n Kind voel dit wanneer 'n hond doodgaan of 'n vriend wegtrek.
items.bron: Paul Ekman Group, 'What is sadness?' (paulekman.com/universal-emotions/what-is-sadness/): the universal trigger is the loss of someone or something important. Both examples are losses.

items.bewering: Trane kom maklik, en party kinders wil eerder 'n rukkie alleen sit. Ander soek juis dadelik iemand op om mee te praat.
items.bron: Frontiers in Psychology 2017, 'Is sadness only one emotion?' (PMC5334320): sadness over a loss is described in terms of tears and withdrawal. Paul Ekman Group: sadness signals a need for comfort from others. Both reactions are documented, so the contrast in the block is true.

items.bewering: Vrees is die gevoel wat jou waarsku dat iets dalk gevaarlik is.
items.bron: APA (apa.org/topics/emotion): a threat brings fear. Harvard Health (health.harvard.edu, stress-response press release): the response prepares a person to face or avoid danger.

items.bewering: Jou hart klop vinniger, en jy haal vinniger asem wanneer jy bang word.
items.bron: Harvard Mental Health Letter, 'How stress harms your physical and psychological health' (health.harvard.edu/press_release/...): after a fright the heart pounds and breathing speeds up, as part of the fight-or-flight response caused by adrenaline. Psychology Tools, 'Fight or flight (CYP)': faster heart rate and rapid breathing.

items.bewering: Kinders voel dit voor 'n toets of in die donker gang by die huis.
items.bron: Nationwide Children's Hospital, 'Helping kids get over their fears' (nationwidechildrens.org), and Cedars-Sinai's matching page: children of school age worry whether they will pass a test, and at 7 fears include dark spaces. Muris et al. 2000 (Maastricht University) found fear of the dark common up to age 9. Fear before a test is strictly closer to worry, but children call it being afraid, and the claim says only that they feel it.

items.bewering: Afguns kom op wanneer iemand anders kry of wen wat jy self wou hê. 'n Klasmaat kry 'n nuwe fiets, en joune is al oud.
items.bron: Parrott & Smith 1993, as summarised in Wikipedia 'Jealousy' and Psychology Today, 'What is the difference between envy and jealousy' (2014): envy arises when a person lacks another's quality, achievement or possession and wants it. 'Kry of wen' covers both possession and achievement, and the bicycle example fits.

items.bewering: Die gevoel is ongemaklik, en baie kinders sê dit nie graag hardop nie.
items.bron: Psychology Today (2014, citing Parrott & Smith): envy brings feelings of inferiority and resentment, and sometimes guilt or shame about feeling envious. That shame is why it is not readily said aloud. Unpleasant: the same source.

items.bewering: Jou beste maat sit elke pouse by die nuwe kind. Jaloesie is die bang gevoel dat jy haar as maat verloor.
items.bron: Parrott (Wikipedia 'Jealousy'; Psychology Today 2014): jealousy arises in a close relationship when a person fears losing an important other to a rival, and its features include fear of loss. A best friend and a new child as the rival is a textbook case. Jealousy is also mixed with hurt and anger, so 'bang gevoel' simplifies, but fear of loss is its defining core.

items.bewering: By afguns wil jy hê wat jy nie het nie. By jaloesie is jy bang om te verloor wat jy wel het.
items.bron: Tested as a set with the Afguns block and the two begrip entries. The 'lack versus loss' contrast is the established one: Parrott & Smith 1993, and Rawls ('jealousy involves the wish to keep what one has, and envy the wish to get what one does not have'), via Wikipedia 'Jealousy'. Observation, not a fault: in the research, what is feared lost is a relationship with a person, not a thing. The sentence on its own ('wat jy wel het') is wider than that, but the friend example just before it and the begrip entry ('jou plek by 'n belangrike mens') narrow it correctly. Parrott also finds the two often come together. The lesson does not deny that.

items.bewering: Baie mense sê 'jaloers' vir albei gevoelens. Afguns is die presiese naam vir die eerste een.
items.bron: Afrikaans: Supertaal's Afrikaans dictionary entry 'jaloers' (gesellig.co.za/t/32331-jaloers/) gives the envy meaning ('negatiewe gevoel veroorsaak deurdat iemand iets het of kan kry wat jy ook wil hê') with 'afgunstig' as a synonym, so jaloers is used for envy. The entry 'afgunstig' (gesellig.co.za/t/38364-afgunstig/) gives 'vol van afguns'. Dutch cognate: woorden.org 'jaloers' gives both meanings, (1) envy and (2) fear of losing a partner to someone else. English: American Heritage Dictionary usage note, 'jealousy and jealous are often used in situations that involve envy'. Source caution: WAT and HAT are behind a login and could not be read, and Supertaal is a community-edited dictionary. Its entry backs the half of the claim that matters (jaloers used for envy). I found no Afrikaans source for the loss meaning, which rests on the Dutch and English sources.

items.bewering: Jou beste maat ... / Afguns is die presiese naam
items.bron: Superlative check. 'Beste maat' is the story's setting, not a claim about the world. 'Presiese' is an absolute ('the exact name'): afguns is the specific word for envy (Supertaal 'afgunstig': 'vol van afguns'; Dutch and English sources above). Read as 'the specific word, compared with the looser jaloers', it holds. No other superlative (eerste, grootste, enigste, altyd, nooit) appears in the lesson.

items.bewering: Baie kinders sê net dat dit goed gaan, en dan hoor niemand wat regtig aangaan nie.
items.blok: Noem die gevoel by sy naam
items.bron: BBC Children in Need / Censuswide survey 2023 (bbcchildreninneed.co.uk, 'the results of our mental health survey'): 26% of 11-18-year-olds regularly feel they must hide how they feel. Action for Children 2022, reported by First News: six in ten children hide their worries from their parents. 'Baie kinders' is supported. The survey ages are older than Gr 4, but the claim is modest.

items.bewering: 'Kwaad', 'bang' en 'teleurgesteld' sê elkeen iets anders oor dieselfde dag. 'Ek is teleurgesteld oor die span se keuse' sê presies wat in jou aangaan.
items.blok: Noem die gevoel by sy naam
items.bron: These are three different emotions (APA: each emotion's character comes from what the event means). Lieberman et al. 2007, 'Putting feelings into words', Psychological Science (UCLA pdf): naming a feeling ('affect labeling') reduces the amygdala's response. Disappointment is defined below. The example sentence names the feeling and its cause, which is what the block claims.

items.bewering: Kwaad word is nie verkeerd nie, en bang wees is ook nie verkeerd nie. Wat jy doen terwyl jy kwaad is, kan wel iemand anders seermaak.
items.blok: Wat jy met die gevoel doen
items.bron: Nemours KidsHealth, 'Taming your temper' (kidshealth.org/en/kids/temper.html): 'Everyone gets angry', 'It's perfectly OK to be angry at times', 'Taking it out on others never solves anything'. North Carolina Early Learning Progressions (earlylearningprogressions.fpg.unc.edu): all feelings are okay, but some behaviours used to express them are not. Cedars-Sinai / Nationwide Children's: fears are a normal part of childhood.

items.bewering: Slaan en skel maak die skade net groter.
items.blok: Wat jy met die gevoel doen
items.bron: Bushman, Baumeister & Stack 1999, JPSP (umich.edu/~bbushman, NYT and Boston Globe reports): venting anger by hitting increased later aggression rather than lowering it. KidsHealth: 'Taking it out on others never solves anything.' The claim concerns the harm between people, and hitting or scolding adds to that harm, so 'net groter' holds.

items.bewering: Dit help dikwels om met 'n grootmens te praat, al maak dit nie die probleem weg nie.
items.blok: Wat jy met die gevoel doen
items.bron: KidsHealth, 'Taming your temper': 'It helps to talk about your anger with an adult' (a parent, teacher or relative). NSPCC/Childline with Place2Be, May 2025 anger advice (nspcc.org.uk): talk to a parent, teacher, friend or Childline. The honest caveat ('al maak dit nie die probleem weg nie') is sound: 'dikwels' (often), not 'altyd' (always).

items.bewering: Lys: 'Sê vir iemand hoe jy voel en waaroor jy so voel.' / 'Stap eers weg en kom terug wanneer jy kalmer is.' / 'Teken of skryf die gevoel op papier neer.' / 'Vra vir hulp wanneer die gevoel te swaar raak.'
items.blok: Maniere om 'n sterk gevoel te wys sonder om iemand seer te maak
items.bron: Tested as a set. Every item is recommended, and none hurts anyone. Talking and asking for help: KidsHealth 'Taming your temper', and NSPCC/Childline + Place2Be 2025. Drawing: KidsHealth ('Draw a picture of how you feel'). Writing: Childline/Place2Be (journaling). Walking away and coming back after calming down: Human Performance Resources by CHAMP, 'Help your kids manage their anger' (hprc-online.org), lists walking away, and its guidance is to talk it through once calm. Observation, not a fault: 'stap weg' is a way to handle the feeling rather than to 'show' it, as the heading says, but nothing in it is false.

items.bewering: Jy kan nie in 'n ander mens se kop inkyk nie. Jy sien sy gesig, jy hoor sy stem, en jy kyk wat hy doen.
items.bron: Barrett et al. 2019 (PSPI; APS release): people read emotion from the face, the voice, behaviour and the context, and no single cue is reliable on its own. 'Kop inkyk' is a figure of speech for direct access to another's mind. The mapping holds.

items.bewering: 'n Maat wat alleen langs die veld sit, sê iets sonder woorde. Jy kan verkeerd raai, en daarom vra jy liewer wat aangaan.
items.bron: Mapping checked. 'Sê iets sonder woorde' means body language carries information, and the next sentence says that information can be misread. Barrett et al. 2019 (Northeastern University report, news.northeastern.edu, 19 July 2019): emotions cannot be read from expression alone, so asking is the sound conclusion. A learner who reasons further is not led to think body language is certain.

items.bewering: Dan nooi jy hom om saam te speel.
items.bron: This is advice, not a factual claim. Inviting a child who sits alone is ordinary prosocial guidance and contradicts no source. Read together with the Hartseer block, which says 'party kinders wil eerder 'n rukkie alleen sit': the sequence ask first, then invite leaves room for the answer, so the two blocks do not contradict each other. Nothing false.

items.bewering: emosie: 'n Gevoel wat vanself in jou opkom en weer wegraak.
items.bron: Same as the study block 'Wat is 'n emosie?', word for word, so it is true when read alone (APA; APA Handbook 'relatively brief episode').

items.bewering: teleurgesteld: Die seer gevoel wanneer iets waarop jy gehoop het nie gebeur nie.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'disappointment': 'the feeling of being sad because something has not happened or been as good, successful, etc.'; Webster's: failure of expectation or hope. Matches.

items.bewering: afguns: Die ongemaklike gevoel wanneer iemand anders kry wat jy self wou hê.
items.bron: Parrott & Smith (Wikipedia 'Jealousy'; Psychology Today 2014); Supertaal 'afgunstig'. Read alone it is true. It leaves out 'wen' (achievement), which the study block includes, but that is shorter, not different.

items.bewering: jaloesie: Die bang gevoel dat iemand jou plek by 'n belangrike mens inneem.
items.bron: Parrott: fear of losing an important other to a rival (Wikipedia 'Jealousy'). Read alone it is true, and it agrees with the study block's friend example and with the loss half of the afguns/jaloesie contrast.

opsomming: Elke kontroleerbare bewering, ook die afguns/jaloesie-kontras wat as 'n stel getoets is en die raad oor kwaad word, is teen gesaghebbende bronne bevestig; die enigste swak grond is dat die Afrikaanse gebruik van 'jaloers' vir afguns net deur 'n gemeenskapswoordeboek (Supertaal) gedek word omdat WAT en HAT agter 'n aanmelding is, en twee klein waarnemings (die 'ná 'n wedstryd'-voorbeeld en die wyer 'wat jy wel het') is nie foute nie.
